scope: Real disk reads of prepared per-method container files (one whole, one chunk_size=256 chunked, written by horizon.town_disk.prepare_case) followed by decode, on this machine only, replaying three deterministic 256x256-viewport trajectories (smooth_walk, boundary_backtrack, teleport) over the synthetic town map. "whole" times horizon.town_disk.load_whole(region=ROI) (decode the whole container, crop an owned copy); "region" times horizon.town_region.load_region (ROI) (read and decode only the chunks the ROI overlaps). The ROI is a real, possibly multi-chunk, viewport window -- not restricted to one exact grid chunk the way horizon.town_disk.load_chunked is. There is no application cache for either arm (see no_appcache_note). bytes_read/bytes_requested/read_calls/seek_calls are the application-level read()/seek() syscall counts the readers themselves tally, not a measurement of physical SSD/controller transfer size.

settings.order_policy: within each (trajectory_kind, repeat) continuous run, a starting parity is tracked per (method, mode) cell: frame 0 of that run uses the current parity, frame 1 the opposite, and so on (swapped = (start_parity + frame_index) % 2), so the measured pair (whole vs. region) alternates every frame. The starting parity itself is flipped once per (trajectory_kind, repeat) run (before frame 0 of the next run), so it also alternates across repeats and across trajectory kinds -- "alternate each frame and trajectory" is satisfied by the combination of the two. Method and mode ordering is not alternated: the outer loops are method, then mode, in the fixed order horizon.codec.METHODS and --modes were given in.
settings.trajectory_policy: Three deterministic trajectory kinds are generated once per run (from the seeded RNG, one independent stream per kind) and reused, unchanged, across every method and mode (same schedule everywhere, like scripts/compare_town_disk.py's region_schedule): (1) smooth_walk -- a momentum random walk (acceleration ~ Normal(0, 8.0), velocity clipped to +/-24 px/step) over `--steps` steps, wandering continuously and crossing many chunk_size=256 boundaries as it drifts across a size>=513 map; (2) boundary_backtrack -- one axis and one interior chunk_size=256 grid line are chosen once, then the viewport center oscillates back and forth across that exact line every step (alternating sign, growing amplitude), repeatedly crossing and re-crossing the same boundary; (3) teleport -- `--steps` independent uniform draws over the full map, no correlation between consecutive positions, the opposite of a smooth walk. Each kind's center-point sequence is mapped to a 256x256 viewport region via clamping (see viewport_policy), then that exact, already-computed region sequence is replayed `--repeats` times per (method, mode) cell for the timing statistics; the positions themselves are never regenerated or perturbed between repeats.
settings.viewport_policy: A trajectory center (center_row, center_col) is mapped to a region (row, col, 256, 256) by row = clamp(center_row - 128, 0, size - 256), col = clamp(center_col - 128, 0, size - 256). With --size >= 513 this never shrinks the viewport (size - 256 >= 257 > 0 always holds), so every frame's region is exactly 256x256; only its row/col offset is clamped at the map edges.
settings.priming_policy: warm_buffered: before the first frame of each (trajectory_kind, repeat) continuous run -- i.e. once per run, not once per frame -- this script does one untimed ordinary buffered read of BOTH the whole container file and the chunked container file for that method, discarding the bytes, so both files are symmetrically warmed before timing starts. It is never repeated mid-run: once a run's frames start being timed, no further priming read happens until the next (trajectory_kind, repeat) run begins. macos_nocache: no priming is performed by this script at all; see no_appcache_note.
settings.validation_policy: Every loaded array, from both arms, on every frame, is checked (exact ndarray type, shape, dtype, byte content against a crop of the original in-memory map) immediately after the call returns -- but after metrics/timing for that call have already been captured by the library function itself, so validation work is never inside a timed span.
settings.no_appcache_note: Neither arm is backed by any application-level cache in this script, horizon.town_disk, or horizon.town_region: every frame, for both arms, opens its container file fresh, reads exactly the bytes it needs, closes it, and decodes -- nothing from one frame (or one repeat, or one trajectory) is reused by the next. "warm_buffered" vs "macos_nocache" is a request about the OS page cache, not a claim about this script's own state, and "warm_buffered" is not a claim of a physically cold read either way: it only means this script primed the OS page cache by reading both files once before timing; "macos_nocache" only means horizon.town_disk/horizon.town_region asked the kernel (fcntl F_NOCACHE) not to retain newly read pages for that descriptor -- neither mode is a verified cold-hardware read (see horizon.town_disk.CACHE_NOTE).
